comp_011:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up a recurring board meeting cadence so our corporate record stays clean and minutes are produced on schedule. Use {{vendor}}, our scheduling tool, through its API or tool interface (MCP if available) with your configured credentials. You should not need the dashboard.

Before you start, ask me for anything missing:
- The cadence: monthly, quarterly, or another interval, and the preferred week and day (for example, second Tuesday of each quarter's first month).
- Meeting length, time zone, and preferred start time.
- Attendee names and emails for directors, observers, and the company secretary or counsel.
- Location or video-conference details.
- The start date and how many occurrences to schedule, or an end date.

Then:
1. Check my connected calendars in {{vendor}} for conflicts across the proposed dates. If an availability schedule for board slots does not exist, create one that reflects my working hours, plus date overrides or out-of-office periods I mention.
2. Create a board meeting event type or recurring booking in {{vendor}}. Use a clear title like "Board of Directors Meeting – [Company]", the agreed duration, and a description noting that minutes will be recorded.
3. Book the recurring series for the agreed occurrences and invite all attendees.
4. If any occurrence conflicts with an existing calendar entry or a holiday, propose the nearest alternative slot. Ask me before rescheduling it.

Done looks like this: a recurring board series exists in {{vendor}}, invitations have gone to every attendee, and no occurrence is double-booked.

Report back with:
- The event or series name and its identifier.
- A table of every scheduled date and time, with time zone.
- The attendee list and whether each invite was sent.
- Any conflicts found and how you resolved them.
- Anything you could not complete and why.

comp_011:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a reusable board meeting minutes template in {{vendor}}, our project-management tool, as part of keeping our board minutes on cadence.

If you don't already have this information, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization details and confirmation you can access it with my configured credentials, (2) the standard board meeting agenda items we use (e.g., call to order, approval of prior minutes, financial update, officer/committee reports, old business, new business, executive session, adjournment), (3) the names/titles of standing attendees (directors, officers, counsel) to pre-list, and (4) where in {{vendor}} our board records should live (a specific project, folder, or space).

Actions to take:
1. In {{vendor}}, use its template feature to start a new document from a pre-built or blank template suited for meeting minutes.
2. Build out the minutes template with sections for: meeting date/time/location, attendees present and absent, quorum confirmation, approval of prior minutes, each standing agenda item I provided, action items with owners, and space for signature/date at the end.
3. Organize this template alongside our other project docs and notes in {{vendor}}, in the folder/space I specified, so it's easy to find each cadence cycle.
4. Name the template clearly (e.g., "Board Meeting Minutes Template") and confirm it can be duplicated for each new meeting without altering the master copy.

Done looks like: a saved, reusable minutes template exists in {{vendor}} in the correct location, containing all standard sections and pre-listed attendees, ready to be duplicated before each board meeting.

Report back with: the location/link of the template within {{vendor}}, a summary of the sections included, and any gaps (e.g., missing agenda items or attendee names) you need me to fill in before it's finalized.

comp_011:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for an upcoming board meeting so the minutes-taking process runs smoothly, even though holding the meeting itself remains a human step. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: the meeting date/time, the video conferencing tool I'll use (e.g., Zoom, Google Meet), the list of directors and any invitees expected to attend, and the agenda items or resolutions to be discussed.
2. Using my existing minutes template (ask me to share the file or its current draft if not already available), pre-fill the header fields: company name, meeting date, meeting type (regular/special), location or dial-in method, and the expected attendee list marked as 'present' or 'absent' placeholders for me to update live.
3. Draft a structured skeleton inside the template with sections for: call to order/quorum confirmation, approval of prior minutes, each agenda item with space for discussion summary and motion/vote/resolution language, and adjournment.
4. Prepare a short checklist for whoever takes notes during the meeting (e.g., capture motions verbatim, record votes by name, note abstentions/recusals, timestamp key decisions).
5. Set a calendar reminder or note for me confirming the meeting is scheduled, so the live session isn't missed.

Done looks like: a ready-to-use minutes template with pre-filled logistics, a clear agenda-mapped skeleton for real-time note capture, and a note-taker checklist — all ready before the meeting starts. Since directors must actually convene, deliberate, and have someone capture what is decided in real time, this remains a human step and I will conduct and record the live meeting myself.

Report back with: the finalized template content (or a summary if the file is long), the checklist, and confirmation of what's ready versus what still needs my input before the meeting.

comp_011:n4.prompt:
You are helping me circulate the latest board meeting minutes for signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature/notarization platform. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) the finalized minutes document (file or data-room link), (2) the full list of signers with names, emails, and roles (e.g., Chair, Secretary, Directors), (3) the required signing order if any, (4) the reminder cadence and expiration/deadline for the signature request, and (5) confirmation of my {{vendor}} account access (use my configured credentials only).

Once you have these, prepare (but do not submit) the signature routing: draft the notarization/signature request in {{vendor}}, attach the minutes document, set the recipient list in the correct signing order, configure automatic reminders, and set the expiration date per my instructions. Produce a clear summary showing: document name and version, full signer list with order, reminder schedule, expiration date, and any special routing notes (e.g., sequential vs. parallel signing).

Because sending this request formally circulates a corporate record and requires explicit human approval before it goes out, do not click send, submit, or finalize the request in {{vendor}} yourself. Present the fully prepared request details and a checklist confirming everything is correct, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft request summary, the checklist, any missing information you had to flag, and a note confirming the request is staged in {{vendor}} awaiting my explicit approval before circulation.

comp_011:n5.prompt:
You are helping me file signed board minutes in our data room, which lives in {{vendor}}. The goal is that every executed set of minutes is stored in the right folder, tagged with useful metadata, free of duplicates, and visible only to the right people.

Ask me for anything missing before you start:
- The signed minutes file(s), as final executed PDFs
- The meeting date and meeting type (regular, special, written consent) for each file
- The data room folder path for board minutes, or confirmation to create one (e.g., Corporate Records / Board Minutes / [Year])
- Who should have access (board members, counsel, investors) and at what level (view-only vs. edit)

Then, using {{vendor}} and your configured credentials:
1. Locate the board minutes folder in the data room. If it doesn't exist, create it under the agreed path.
2. Search the folder for existing minutes from the same meeting date to avoid duplicates. If you find a match, show me both and ask whether to replace, keep a new version, or skip.
3. Upload each signed file with a consistent name, e.g., "YYYY-MM-DD Board Minutes - [Type] - Signed.pdf". Use a resumable or chunked upload for large files if {{vendor}} supports it.
4. Set custom metadata or properties on each file where supported: meeting date, meeting type, signed status = signed, filed date.
5. Check folder sharing. Confirm access matches what I specified, with view-only links and download controls for diligence viewers. Flag anything broader than expected, and don't widen access without asking me.
6. Confirm the file's version history is available, so earlier revisions can be recovered.

You're done when every signed file is in the correct folder, named and tagged consistently, with no duplicates and correct permissions.

Report back with a short table showing file name, folder path, meeting date, metadata set (yes/no), and who has access. Below the table, list any issues, open questions, or files you skipped.
